title: The demo worked because every incident followed the template.
body:
The demo worked because every incident followed the template. Real SRE traffic didn't.

The POC was clean: ~20 users, incidents that mostly matched the structured format. My retrieval and resolution-step generation leaned on that structure — pull the right fields, ground the LLM, surface the similar incident.

Then it met 200+ SREs and years of real ServiceNow history. Teams hadn't filled the incident format consistently — fields skipped, freeform where I expected structure, structure where there wasn't any. The assumptions that made the notebook version look smart were the exact thing buckling at scale.

The fix wasn't a better parser. I went back through the actual data, found ~6-month windows where teams had genuinely been consistent, anchored on those, and designed the pipeline to tolerate the drift instead of pretending it away.

A notebook proves the idea works on the data you picked. Real traffic tells you which of your assumptions were load-bearing.
